name: Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy
summary: Physiotherapy improves balance, strength, walking and foot protection and supports pain management; patients must learn foot checks and safe exercise because sensation loss can hide injuries.

looksLike: Foot sensation with monofilament and vibration
redFlags: Open ulcer, infection or a hot swollen foot (possible Charcot foot)
Blackened or very pale, cold toes
Sudden severe pain or new weakness
firstSteps: Check feet, sensation and footwear, and ask about ulcers and blood sugar.
Teach daily foot inspection and start gentle, safe exercise.

assess: Foot sensation with monofilament and vibration
measures: Berg Balance Scale or single-leg stand

stages.goal: Loss of sensation allows injuries to go unnoticed, so foot protection and daily checks are as important as exercise.

dose: Balance training: 10 to 15 minutes, 3 or more times a week near support.
Strength training: 2 to 3 sets of 8 to 12 repetitions, 2 to 3 days a week.
Aerobic exercise: 150 minutes a week at moderate effort if well tolerated, in suitable footwear.
